title: librarian-core-loop
intention: The core resolve-or-generate loop (cairn/devices/librarian/loop.py): always the graph first. A question embeds and walks the tree; if the best cosine clears RESOLUTION_FLOOR the walk IS the answer — no inference. On a miss, the LLM is asked for NODES (never the answer); they deposit through the same provenance gate; the ORIGINAL question resubmits, and the proof the backfill worked is that structure now resolves it. The backfill-cache livelock is fixed as physics AT the junction, as the loop goes live: (1) the backfill prompt carries tree_state's digest + the nearest already-known nodes, so 'same question, changed graph' canonicalizes to a DIFFERENT cache key; (2) a round depositing nothing fresh terminates loudly as no_progress instead of spinning with the trap booked as savings.
why: Akien's ruling, 2026-07-27, verbatim: 'The librarian ALWAYS reaches for the graph trees, and if the graph tree can't, the LLM is used to backfill it until it can.' And the load-bearing clause: 'escalate on graph failure to a node depositing call THAT VALIDATES BY RESUBMITTING THE SAME REQUEST.' This is Law 1 as a runtime mechanism — the resolver spent on the novel, every answered question becoming structure — and it is the heart every librarian face (learn, summarize, chat) beats on.
traces_to: Law 1 — the answer path is a graph walk; inference fires only to EXTEND structure, and the second crossing of the same ground is walk-only (measured: backfills 1 -> 0)
Law 3 — RESOLUTION_FLOOR=0.65 is a LABELED n=1 guess, returned in every verdict so no caller mistakes the threshold for settled; UNRESOLVED is a measured outcome, not an error
Law 7 — a refused backfill node rides the verdict whole; no_progress and exhausted terminate loudly; every crossing breadcrumbs RESOLVED and UNRESOLVED alike
Law 8 — a hollow loop (generate answer returned, livelock reopened, progress gate absent) cannot pass the teeth

falsifier.proves_green: proof gate: cairn/devices/librarian/proofs/test_librarian_loop.py (10 teeth) under the tester's MEASURED netns seal — validations/test_librarian_loop.json, green, sealed; trees re-sealed the same run (tree_state landed in trees.py, so its prior seal's horizon expired — a NEW dated entry, 14 teeth now). Build gate: inspected at the PROVEME exit. Durability: committed + pushed.
falsifier.proves_red: RED on any of: the loop returning a generate answer instead of a walk (the host in the answer path); two backfill prompts for the same question against a CHANGED graph canonicalizing to the SAME cache key (the livelock reopened — the proof pins canonicalize inequality); a no-progress round spinning instead of terminating; a refusal at the deposit door dropped from the verdict; loop.py growing an import outside its allowlist. WRONG-SHAPE SIGNAL: UNRESOLVED crossings booked anywhere as savings — the exact relabeling the livelock spec warned about.
falsifier.horizon: re-read when the learn verb / shelving lands on top of it (parent edge b), or when live use accumulates enough verdicts to tune RESOLUTION_FLOOR past n=1.
